features: Public link to the live round score with no registration required for viewers
One player runs the round and all others stay in sync automatically
Final round card ready to share to any messenger in one tap
Group round history with a season leaderboard visible only to your regular crew
Live hole comments from playing partners via the browser
antiFeatures: No requirement for all participants to register
No social features locked behind a subscription
No forced app download just to view the score
golf-3.monetization: Players in Golf GameBook and TheGrint already pay specifically for live group scoring. The target market is regular groups that play together every weekend. One paying organizer at $5 to $8 per month brings along five occasional users.

golf-4.title: Progress Analytics for the Self-Taught Golfer
golf-4.oneLiner: A personal round breakdown showing exactly where you are losing strokes and what to practice next week
golf-4.gap: A player sees final stats but has no idea what to do with them. Strokes gained shows a number but does not say which practice drill will eliminate that deficit
golf-4.pitch: After every round the service produces one specific takeaway: "you are losing 1.4 strokes on approaches from 80 to 100 yards" and one concrete practice task for the next session. Over a season this builds a personal progress map that replaces a coach for the self-taught player. The paying customer is someone who already spent $1,000 on clubs but does not take lessons.
features: One takeaway after each round: the main area of loss, no data overload
A specific practice task with a drill description and a clear goal
Progress map by zone: putting, approaches, long game, bunker play
Comparison against a player at your own handicap, not a tour professional
Task history with a completion log so you can see the practice-to-result connection
antiFeatures: No dashboard overload with charts that do not drive any action
No comparison with tour players that discourages beginners
No AI caddy club recommendations without actual distance data on the player
golf-4.monetization: Arccos charges $200 per year for tracking alone. Players pay precisely because they want to lower their handicap, as the reviews make clear. A service without hardware (manual entry or import from existing apps) can charge $50 to $80 per year and serve players who do not have sensors.

golf-5.title: Offline Maps for Courses Without Cell Service
golf-5.oneLiner: A GPS rangefinder that works without an internet connection on any remote or rural course
golf-5.gap: A player drives out to a countryside or mountain course with no signal. The app loaded maps during setup, but without internet the GPS shows nothing or displays a blank screen
golf-5.pitch: The service downloads vector course maps to the device when you add a course to favorites, and on the course itself it runs fully offline: GPS, hole switching, scoring, and distances with zero data usage. The target market is countryside, mountain, and rural courses, which make up the majority in Europe and Russia. Sold as a one-time purchase per course or a subscription for players with several favorite courses.
features: Complete offline course map with the green, water hazards, and bunkers
GPS distances with no internet connection using the device's native module
Automatic hole switching by GPS position with no screen tap required
Bulk pre-download by region, favorite courses, or upcoming trip
Minimal battery drain because there are no constant network requests
antiFeatures: No dependency on Google Maps or the freshness of their satellite imagery
No forced online check required to start a round
No ads or upgrade pop-ups during play
golf-5.monetization: The audience is players at off-the-grid courses who are frustrated by exactly this problem. An offline course pack sells for $2 to $5, or an unlimited-courses subscription for $30 per year. Additional revenue from B2B deals with the courses themselves, who want to offer guests an app that actually works.

golf-6.title: Pocket Caddy Based on Your Real Distances
golf-6.oneLiner: Club recommendations built on your actual carry distances, the wind, and the terrain, not tour averages
golf-6.gap: AI caddies in existing apps recommend clubs based on abstract norms, ignoring the fact that this particular player hits a 6-iron 130 yards, not 175
golf-6.pitch: The service builds a personal distance profile for each club from 10 to 15 rounds and uses that profile when making suggestions. Recommendations factor in wind, elevation change, and pin position, but the primary variable is always the player's own history. The paying customer already believes in data (they have probably tried Arccos) but is disappointed by the quality of advice.
features: Personal distance calibration by club over the first few rounds
Club suggestion with reasoning: "your 8-iron carries 115, pin is 108, wind into you"
Elevation adjustment: uphill or downhill adds or removes a club
Suggestion history with a note on whether the ball went where intended, to refine the model
Works without sensors: player enters the result manually and the model updates itself
antiFeatures: No generic average-based suggestions before personal calibration is complete
No analytics overload: one suggestion per shot, not a menu of five options
No absurd recommendations like "driver then two chips" on a par 4
golf-6.monetization: Players with a handicap between 10 and 25 already pay for Arccos ($200) and SwingU, but the core frustration is specifically the quality of advice. The service can live as a layer that accepts history imported from Arccos and charge $40 to $60 per year for better recommendations rather than for tracking.

golf-7.title: B2B Analytics Tool for Golf Clubs
golf-7.oneLiner: A dashboard for course managers: pace of play, hole congestion, and guest stats in real time
golf-7.gap: A course manager has no idea where bottlenecks form on the course, why pace of play drops on Fridays, or which holes generate the most guest complaints
golf-7.pitch: The service collects anonymous data from players' apps and turns it into an operational dashboard for the course: a pace-of-play heat map by hole, a congestion forecast for the next day, and a ranking of the course's pinch points. The club pays monthly while players use a free scoring and navigation app as the data collection layer. This is a B2B SaaS sold through the course manager.
features: Real-time pace-of-play heat map by hole
Next-day course congestion forecast based on historical data and tee-time bookings
Hole rankings by complaints and delays with marshaling recommendations
Anonymous guest report: origin, handicap range, and return frequency
Free player app as the data collection point for the course
antiFeatures: No selling of player personal data without their consent
No charging the player for features the course needs
No complex installation: the course does not set up any hardware
golf-7.monetization: Golf clubs already pay for tee-sheet systems like ForeUp, Lightspeed Golf, and Jonas at $200 to $800 per month. Course analytics as an add-on module at $100 to $300 per month is realistic. First customers are reached through golf course associations that represent 15,000 courses in the US alone.

intermittent-fasting-1.title: Post-Surgery Protocol
intermittent-fasting-1.oneLiner: A structured intermittent fasting plan for people recovering from bariatric surgery, coordinated with their surgeon.
intermittent-fasting-1.gap: After bariatric surgery, patients go home with a single sheet of paper and advice to eat less. They have no idea when or how to introduce a fasting window, they are afraid of damaging their stitches, and regular apps know nothing about their anatomy.
intermittent-fasting-1.pitch: Bariatric patients pay tens of thousands for nutritional rehabilitation programs, then are left alone with their plate the moment they are discharged. This service gives them a step-by-step 12-week fasting plan aligned with their healing stages, plus chat access to a nutritionist who specializes in post-operative eating. Clinics plug the product in as an extension of their aftercare and pay for it as a B2B add-on.
features: A 12-week transition plan from liquids to solid foods, with a gradual introduction of the fasting window
Weekly video calls with a nutritionist experienced in bariatric protocols
Symptom tracker covering nausea, reflux, and dumping syndrome, with automatic summaries sent to the physician
Recipe library organized by phase (pureed, soft, regular) with protein per serving calculated
Clinic integration: the surgeon can view patient progress and adjust the plan through a dedicated physician dashboard
antiFeatures: Gamification and streaks: someone recovering from surgery should not feel like a failure if their fasting window shifts
Letting users pick long protocols without nutritionist approval
Photo-based calorie scanning: post-operative portions require precision, not rough estimates
intermittent-fasting-1.monetization: Clinics pay a subscription to enroll their patients (B2B). Patients pay the nutritionist directly for 3 to 6 sessions in the first month. Bariatric centers already sell aftercare programs for significant sums, and this is a natural extension of that same service.

intermittent-fasting-2.title: Fasting for Shift Workers
intermittent-fasting-2.oneLiner: An adaptive intermittent fasting plan for people with rotating schedules: nurses, security guards, drivers, factory operators.
intermittent-fasting-2.gap: A person works a rotating two-on-two-off or 24-hour shift pattern. Their night and morning fall on different clock hours every week. Every existing app wants the same eating window at the same time every day, which is physically impossible for shift workers.
intermittent-fasting-2.pitch: Shift workers make up a third of the employed population, and they face a higher risk of metabolic disorders precisely because of their irregular eating rhythm. This service takes the week's shift schedule and automatically shifts the fasting window so it fits their real day: eat after the shift, fast during sleep. Employers in healthcare and transport pay for the program as a corporate wellness benefit that reduces sick days.
features: Shift schedule import (manual entry or a link to a corporate scheduling tool)
Automatic fasting window adjustment for each workday, no manual tweaking needed
Body education content adapted to the time of day the shift falls, not generic morning framing
Sleep and fatigue tracker alongside the eating window, showing how fasting affects recovery after a night shift
HR dashboard for employers: aggregate department stats with no personal data exposed
antiFeatures: A fixed 16:8 preset with no flexibility: useless for shift workers
Push notifications at the same time every day: if someone is sleeping after a night shift, that is a failure
Daily streaks: a shift worker's rhythm is per-shift, not per-day
intermittent-fasting-2.monetization: Corporate contracts with hospitals, factories, and transport companies, which already buy wellness programs for staff. Individual subscriptions for shift workers who pay out of pocket at a lower price than the corporate tier. Partnerships with healthcare worker unions.

intermittent-fasting-3.title: Medically Supervised Fasting
intermittent-fasting-3.oneLiner: A clinically oriented service for people with prediabetes and insulin resistance: a fasting protocol with glucose monitoring and an endocrinologist coach.
intermittent-fasting-3.gap: An endocrinologist says try intermittent fasting and books a follow-up three months out. The patient has no idea where to start, is afraid of hypoglycemia, and no app knows anything about their lab results.
intermittent-fasting-3.pitch: More than 20 million people in Russia have prediabetes, and half of them have already been told to try time-restricted eating. This service takes their lab results, including fasting glucose, HbA1c, and insulin, and builds a safe fasting plan with weekly reviews by an endocrinologist coach. The patient pays less than a private clinic visit and arrives at their doctor's appointment with three months of data already logged.
features: Lab result upload (PDF or photo) with automatic calculation of a safe starting fasting window
Integration with continuous glucose monitors (CGM): see blood sugar response to the eating window in real time
Weekly 25-minute video review with an endocrinologist coach
Alert when glucose goes outside a safe range, with a recommendation to break the fast
Physician report: a PDF with one month of trends, ready to bring to an appointment
antiFeatures: Letting users choose long protocols (36 hours or more) without coach approval
Leaderboards and competition with other users
Photo-based food scanning instead of precise entry: managing blood glucose requires gram-level accuracy, not guesses
intermittent-fasting-3.monetization: Subscription with a coach, paid by patients already motivated by their diagnosis. Partnerships with CGM manufacturers (Libre, Dexcom) as recommended software. Corporate contracts with insurance companies as an early prevention program.

intermittent-fasting-4.title: Corporate Fasting Program
intermittent-fasting-4.oneLiner: A weight management program through intermittent fasting for corporate clients: HR buys it, employees use it, results are measurable.
intermittent-fasting-4.gap: Corporate wellness comes down to a gym discount that 4 percent of employees actually use. The employer pays and sees no result. Fasting requires no gym and works even for people with desk jobs.
intermittent-fasting-4.pitch: Companies spend money on health insurance and wellness programs, but HR has no tool that shows a measurable outcome in lost pounds or reduced sick days. This service is sold to HR as a 12-week company challenge with anonymous group stats, live nutritionist webinars, and a weekly team progress digest. Employees get structure and peer support. Employers get a report.
features: Team dashboard for HR with aggregate metrics and no personal data: participation rate, average fasting duration by week
12-week program with weekly group webinars from a nutritionist
Anonymous team chat where participants support each other without sharing personal numbers
Final employer report with an ROI estimate based on self-reported health metric changes
3-minute onboarding: the employee sees their first timer right away, no long questionnaire
antiFeatures: Named individual leaderboards: creates pressure and violates privacy
Mandatory integration with HRMS systems: drags the sales cycle out by months
Shame-based notifications for missed days: toxic in a corporate context
intermittent-fasting-4.monetization: Corporate team subscription, tapping existing wellness budgets that companies already spend on health insurance, gym benefits, and corporate coaching. Per-employee monthly pricing with a minimum 3-month contract. Employers in Russia already pay for comparable weight loss programs through health insurance.

intermittent-fasting-5.title: Fasting for Older Adults
intermittent-fasting-5.oneLiner: An intermittent fasting program for people over 60, with weekly calls from a real nutritionist and a simple interface with no widgets.
intermittent-fasting-5.gap: Older adults do not carry their phone around and forget to tap the button. Smartwatches do not sync or are not there at all. Modern app interfaces are designed for 30-year-olds. A nutritionist by phone is expensive, and what a grandparent needs is a real human on the other end, not a bot.
intermittent-fasting-5.pitch: The older adult market for intermittent fasting is large and almost entirely unserved: a cardiologist or endocrinologist usually recommends fasting to them, they are willing to pay for personal guidance, and they do not need complex features. The service is built around one weekly call with a nutritionist, a tracker with three buttons (start, stop, log water), and reminders by SMS not just push notifications.
features: Three-action tracker: start the fast, end the fast, log water. Nothing else.
Weekly call with a nutritionist by phone, not just video, because the voice matters to this audience
SMS reminders as a backup channel for when the phone is sitting on the table
A simple printed weekly progress summary to bring to a doctor's appointment
Shared access for an adult child: a son or daughter can see a parent's progress and message the nutritionist
antiFeatures: Widgets and complex setup: older adults do not know what a widget is and will not figure it out
Photo-based food scanning: blurry results and the output is wrong anyway
Gamification and streaks: an older adult whose streak resets will not come back
intermittent-fasting-5.monetization: Subscription paid by an adult child as a gift to their parent, a pattern that already works in telemedicine and grocery delivery. Direct payment by the older user themselves, an audience that is financially comfortable and used to paying for a doctor. Partnerships with cardiology and endocrinology clinics.

intermittent-fasting-6.title: Extended Fasting with Medical Oversight
intermittent-fasting-6.oneLiner: An online program for people practicing multi-day fasts (48 to 72 hours or more) with medical supervision and live support.
intermittent-fasting-6.gap: Someone wants to do a 3-to-5-day fast, has read Longo and Fung, but no tracker handles windows that long and no doctor wants to supervise it. They go it alone and they are scared.
intermittent-fasting-6.pitch: The extended fasting market is growing fast in Europe and the US: retreats running 5 to 10 days cost a lot, and people want to do it at home. This service offers a medically supervised multi-day fasting program without the travel: a doctor reviews baseline labs, daily check-ins happen in the app, an alert fires if dangerous symptoms appear, and a refeeding protocol walks them out of the fast. It is a fraction of the retreat cost and far safer than going solo.
features: Medical onboarding: lab upload (electrolytes, ECG for those over 50), with clearance granted or a recommendation against proceeding
Daily check-in with a symptom log covering weakness, dizziness, heart palpitations, and mood
Early-exit algorithm: automatic alert to the physician when a combination of warning symptoms appears
Refeeding protocol after a long fast with a step-by-step menu for 3 to 7 days
Group chat for each cohort: people fasting at the same time support each other in real time
antiFeatures: Selling multi-day protocols without medical clearance: legally and ethically unacceptable
Gamifying fast duration: competing over who fasts longest is dangerous
Auto-approving any request without checking lab results
intermittent-fasting-6.monetization: The program is sold as a one-time purchase like a course: clearance plus 5-day supervision plus a refeeding protocol. Retreats and clinics already charge large amounts for the same thing offline. The price anchor is a retreat versus the program at a fraction of the cost.

intermittent-fasting-7.title: Fasting as an Insurance Metric
intermittent-fasting-7.oneLiner: A platform for insurance companies: verified fasting protocol adherence data as the basis for a health insurance discount.
intermittent-fasting-7.gap: Insurance gives a discount for a healthy lifestyle but has no way to verify it. A person says they run, but the insurer has no proof. Fasting is objectively verifiable through biomarkers like ketones and glucose, plus tracker data.
intermittent-fasting-7.pitch: Insurance companies are looking for measurable behavioral data to differentiate premiums and cut claims. This service provides a verified quarterly report on fasting protocol adherence, using CGM data or home ketone test strips as objective confirmation. The insurer gets an evidence-based risk management tool. The insured gets a discount on their policy. Both sides already pay for something similar, separating healthy from unhealthy policyholders.
features: Fasting verification through home ketone test strips with timestamped photo confirmation
Quarterly report in insurer-ready format: weeks on protocol, average duration, gaps
Integration with health insurance tiers: the insurer sees aggregate cohort metrics for their policyholders
5-minute onboarding for the insured: no long questionnaire, just choose a protocol and upload a policy number
Partner dashboard for the insurer: cohort management and configurable thresholds for the discount
antiFeatures: Giving the insurer direct access to an individual's personal data without explicit consent
Requiring a continuous glucose monitor with no alternative: too high a barrier for most people
Leaderboards among policyholders: creates unhealthy pressure
intermittent-fasting-7.monetization: The insurer pays for cohort enrollment (B2B, with existing budgets for policyholder health management programs). The insured pays for a verification kit of test strips as a consumable. Comparable programs already operate in the US through major insurers.

cycling-1.title: Safe Bike Route
cycling-1.oneLiner: Navigation that plans routes only along bike paths and quiet streets, never on highways
cycling-1.gap: Every route planner defaults to the shortest path and sends cyclists onto high-speed roads, shoulders, and closed streets. No service treats road safety as more important than arrival time.
cycling-1.pitch: The app builds routes exclusively on bike lanes, residential streets, and low-speed roads. The rider sets an acceptable risk level, and the algorithm filters out highways, expressways, and paths through private property. Target users: urban commuter cyclists and touring riders who do not want to risk their lives to save five minutes.
features: Safety rating for every road segment (bike lane, residential street, highway, shoulder)
Filters for bike-lane-only routes and highway avoidance during planning
Crowdsourced hazard markers contributed by the community
Offline maps with pre-downloaded routes and real-time voice guidance without delay
Custom start point selection so you are not locked to your current location
antiFeatures: Social feed and friends activity stream
Segment comparisons and speed leaderboards
Workout and power tracking
cycling-1.monetization: Commuter cyclists pay a monthly subscription for offline maps and up-to-date road safety data. B2B: tour operators and bike rental companies pay for a white-label version and an API to embed in their own apps.

cycling-2.title: Reliable Ride Recording
cycling-2.oneLiner: A tracker that records your entire ride without gaps, even with the screen off or while switching apps
cycling-2.gap: Cyclists lose full rides because the operating system suspends the app when the screen turns off. After a two-hour ride they find either a blank track or a straight line cutting through buildings.
cycling-2.pitch: A background tracker that runs as a system service, protected from battery killers on both Android and iOS. GPS points are written to local storage every second so the track survives crashes, network drops, and app switches. The product solves one core need: record the whole ride.
features: Background recording as a foreground service with a persistent notification the system cannot kill
Every GPS point saved locally in real time so nothing is lost on crash
Adaptive battery mode: fewer points on straight segments, more on corners
Automatic GPS recovery after signal loss with flagged gaps in the track
Export to GPX, FIT, and KML without a subscription
antiFeatures: Route planner
Social features and activity feed
Training plans and coaching
cycling-2.monetization: One-time app purchase with no subscription. Optional cloud track storage for those who want sync across devices.

cycling-3.title: Cycling Club Platform
cycling-3.oneLiner: A tool for cycling club organizers: plan group rides, manage schedules, track attendance, and share a club route library
cycling-3.gap: Cycling club coaches run their groups through messaging apps and spreadsheets. No dedicated tool exists for planning group outings, collecting RSVPs, storing the club route archive, and tracking attendance.
cycling-3.pitch: A B2B platform for cycling clubs: the coach creates a ride with a route, members sign up in one place, and after the ride all tracks are collected into a shared club history. Clubs already pay for organization, gear, and insurance, so the payment habit is established.
features: Group ride creation with route, date, difficulty level, and participant cap
Shared club route library with ratings and coach notes
Attendance tracking and participation history for each club member
Ride chat with automatic notifications for cancellations or changes
Strava integration to import participant tracks into the shared history
antiFeatures: Individual training plans
Power and physiology analysis
Route planner for solo rides
cycling-3.monetization: Club subscription for up to 30 members, with a higher tier for unlimited size. Clubs with 20 or more active members already spend more on venue fees, so the price point is not an obstacle.

cycling-4.title: Indoor Training Without Zwift
cycling-4.oneLiner: A smart trainer app that launches in ten seconds and does not demand gigabyte updates before every ride
cycling-4.gap: Smart trainer owners spend 15 to 30 minutes connecting devices and waiting for updates before each workout. Zwift and Rouvy require up to 3 GB for a single update and frequently freeze mid-ride, killing motivation.
cycling-4.pitch: A minimal indoor cycling client: open it, the trainer connects automatically, press start. Updates download silently in the background with no forced interruption before a session. You pay for reliability, not for a virtual world with an avatar.
features: Automatic reconnection to the trainer on Bluetooth drop
Background updates that never block the start of a workout
Structured workouts (intervals, climbs, VO2max) with trainer resistance control
Lightweight real-road video routes without heavy 3D graphics
Support for all ANT+ and Bluetooth sensors regardless of brand
antiFeatures: Multiplayer races and avatar worlds
Gamification and achievement badges
Social feed and ride comments
cycling-4.monetization: Monthly subscription at a price well below Zwift and Rouvy, whose users have already demonstrated willingness to pay for indoor cycling software.

cycling-5.title: Bike Fleet Management for Rental Shops
cycling-5.oneLiner: A CRM for bike rental businesses: track bikes, bookings, maintenance, and curated guest routes
cycling-5.gap: Bike rental shops in tourist towns run on paper logbooks, WhatsApp chats, and Excel sheets. No dedicated tool handles fleet tracking, automated service reminders, and online booking with payment.
cycling-5.pitch: A web service for bike rentals: every bike has a card with full service history, customers book and pay online, and a curated route is included in the booking confirmation. On return, the system logs mileage and schedules the next service automatically. Rental operators already pay for location, inventory, and insurance, so the payment habit is there.
features: Bike card with maintenance history, odometer reading, and planned part replacements
Online booking with payment and automatic confirmation
Guest route cards delivered by QR code at pickup
Service reminders triggered by mileage or calendar date
Dashboard showing fleet utilization, revenue, and popular routes
antiFeatures: Athlete workout tracking
Power and physiology analysis
Social network for cyclists
cycling-5.monetization: Business subscription up to 20 bikes, with a higher tier for unlimited fleet size. Additional revenue from a small commission on online bookings processed through the platform.

cycling-6.title: Gravel Navigator with Real Surface Data
cycling-6.oneLiner: A route planner for gravel cyclists that knows the surface type of every segment and filters by terrain
cycling-6.gap: Gravel riders plan routes blind: neither Komoot nor Bikemap shows actual ground conditions. You only discover on the road that a beautiful forest trail on the map turned into an impassable muddy mess after rain.
cycling-6.pitch: A dedicated planner for gravel and off-road riding: every road segment is colored by surface type (pavement, dirt, gravel, grass) using crowdsourced data and satellite imagery. A filter by bike type and allowed surfaces eliminates surprises on the route. Gravel riders spend heavily on gear, so paying for accurate navigation is a natural fit.
features: Surface-type map layer with up-to-date community data
Route filter by allowed surfaces for a specific bike
Seasonal warnings for segments that become impassable after rain or in winter
User track uploads with surface tagging
Offline maps for remote areas without mobile coverage
antiFeatures: Training plans and fitness analysis
Social network and result comparisons
Navigation for urban commuter routes
cycling-6.monetization: Monthly or annual subscription. Additional PRO tier for gravel event organizers covering route preparation and GPX export for participants.

cycling-7.title: Bike Maintenance Log and Diagnostics
cycling-7.oneLiner: A personal logbook for your bike: part replacement reminders based on mileage, full service history, and links to compatible parts
cycling-7.gap: Cyclists forget to replace chains, brake pads, and lubricant because no one actually tracks mileage per component and sends a reminder. A cycling computer or Strava logs kilometers but never connects them to the lifespan of specific consumable parts.
cycling-7.pitch: A logbook app for your bike: enter the model and components once, mileage syncs from Strava or is entered manually, and the app tells you when to replace the chain, service the fork, and check the brakes. Partner shops can show the exact replacement parts right inside the service reminder notification.
features: Bike card listing all components with their mileage limits
Mileage sync from Strava and manual entry
Replacement reminders with mileage and date thresholds
Full maintenance log: what was replaced, when, where, and at what cost
Compatible parts finder with links to partner shops
antiFeatures: Navigation and route planning
Workout and fitness analysis
Social features and peer comparisons
cycling-7.monetization: One-time purchase. Affiliate revenue from partner parts shops at a percentage of each purchase made through in-app links. Cyclists who invest heavily in their equipment spend regularly on maintenance.

food-delivery-1.title: Refund on Autopilot
food-delivery-1.oneLiner: An automated dispute service for delivery platforms: the customer taps "never arrived", the system gathers evidence and fights for a refund from DoorDash, Uber Eats, or Deliveroo on their behalf
food-delivery-1.gap: A courier marks an order as delivered, the food never arrives, and the platform points to its own GPS stamp and denies the claim. The customer spends an hour in a bot loop and gives up.
food-delivery-1.pitch: The user connects their delivery account and the service automatically documents discrepancies between GPS data, delivery timestamps, chat history, and photos, then files a dispute in the format each platform is required to process. Revenue comes from a percentage of recovered funds. The audience already pays for delivery and wants to receive what they paid for.
features: OAuth connection to DoorDash, Uber Eats, Deliveroo, and Just Eat accounts
Automatic evidence collection: courier tracking screenshot, delivery timestamp, chat history
Complaint template generated to match each platform's dispute process
Automated escalation to support chat with retry logic
Dashboard of successful refunds and per-platform statistics
antiFeatures: No own couriers or delivery infrastructure
No subscription required to access core features
No manual evidence entry by the user
food-delivery-1.monetization: 20% success fee on recovered amounts. The customer already paid for food they never received and is willing to share a cut to get the money back. B2B: corporate clients pay a flat monthly fee for automated order auditing.

food-delivery-2.title: Hot Guarantee
food-delivery-2.oneLiner: A food delivery subscription with one real promise: food arrives hot or you get a full refund, no questions asked, because partner restaurants use dedicated single-order couriers
food-delivery-2.gap: Platforms assign three or four orders to the same courier at once, so your meal sits in a bag for fifty minutes while they drop off everyone else's. There is no refund for cold food.
food-delivery-2.pitch: A network of partner restaurants within three kilometers, each bound by contract to one courier per order with no parallel pickups. Subscribers get guaranteed hot delivery in twenty to twenty-five minutes. Restaurants pay for the listing and the traffic. Customers pay for certainty. Margins are higher because there are no promo subsidies and no error credits to hand out.
features: Map of restaurants with a hot-delivery guarantee within a three-kilometer radius
Dedicated courier per order with no concurrent pickups
Automatic 100% refund if the guarantee is broken, verified by a temperature sensor in the bag or customer rating
Transparent tracking showing the courier is heading only to you
Monthly subscription with a set number of guaranteed deliveries
antiFeatures: No delivery from any restaurant in the city
No promo codes or welcome discounts
No courier batching to cut costs
food-delivery-2.monetization: Monthly customer subscription, similar to Amazon Prime for delivery. Listing fee from restaurants for access to subscribers. Restaurants already pay DoorDash 30% and are willing to pay less for better-quality traffic.

food-delivery-3.title: Lunch for the Whole Office
food-delivery-3.oneLiner: A B2B platform for group office orders: one bill, one courier, one trip. Each employee picks their own meal and the company pays with a single invoice.
food-delivery-3.gap: Twenty people in an office want to eat together, but everyone orders separately through their personal apps. Accounting does not accept twenty separate receipts, and coordinating a shared order in a group chat is a mess.
food-delivery-3.pitch: A company connects a payment method and employees receive a link to a shared order. Everyone adds their meal from the restaurant menu, the system compiles a combined order and issues one corporate invoice broken down by employee. Restaurants get a large order without going through an aggregator. Companies get a single receipt for meal expense reimbursement.
features: Corporate account with team management and per-person spending limits
Shared order link with a collection deadline
Single invoice with per-employee breakdown for accounting
Integration with corporate cards and expense reimbursement systems
Restaurant ratings based on how reliably they handle group orders
antiFeatures: No delivery for individual consumers
No personal promos or cashback
No takeout or pickup options
food-delivery-3.monetization: Monthly per-company subscription priced by headcount. Restaurant commission for group order traffic set below the standard aggregator rate (15% instead of 30%). Companies already spend on corporate meals through catering or individual reimbursements.

food-delivery-4.title: A Human on the Line
food-delivery-4.oneLiner: A delivery service with a live agent instead of a chatbot: a real person is available in your messenger from the moment you place an order until it reaches your door, resolving issues in real time
food-delivery-4.gap: When something goes wrong, whether the food is missing, delivered to the wrong address, or spoiled, the customer lands in a chatbot loop and never reaches a live agent. The problem never gets resolved.
food-delivery-4.pitch: A small network of partner restaurants with a guarantee of live support for every order. An agent in Telegram or WhatsApp sees your order, the courier's location, and the full history in real time. If anything goes wrong, they call the courier or the restaurant and resolve the issue before closing the chat. For customers with chronic conditions, elderly people, and those recovering from surgery, this kind of service is infrastructure, not a luxury.
features: Live agent in a messenger app assigned to every order
Agent sees courier tracking and restaurant history in real time
Instant refund or replacement without forms or waiting
Saved preference history and delivery instructions for returning customers
Priority queue for regulars
antiFeatures: No fully automated order processing
No delivery from any restaurant in the city
No AI assistant for meal recommendations
food-delivery-4.monetization: Premium subscription with live order support. Core audience includes elderly users, post-surgery patients, people with chronic conditions, and families with young children. They already pay for delivery and suffer the most when refund requests are denied.

food-delivery-5.title: Honest Ratings
food-delivery-5.oneLiner: An independent restaurant rating for food delivery based on real customer reviews, not inflated platform stars. Revenue comes from a restaurant analytics subscription.
food-delivery-5.gap: Platforms hide written reviews and inflate star ratings. Choosing a restaurant has become a lottery: five stars and the food arrives cold and wrong.
food-delivery-5.pitch: An independent review aggregator for delivery restaurants: data collected from open sources like Google Maps, Yelp, and App Store reviews, filtered through a review-manipulation detector, and ranked by real quality. Restaurants pay for reputation analytics and competitor benchmarking. Customers use it for free and stop falling for fake star counts.
features: Review aggregation from multiple sources with deduplication
Manipulation detector that flags unusual spikes in five-star reviews within a week
Honest ratings broken down by category: food temperature, delivery speed, order completeness
Restaurant analytics panel showing where they lose customers compared to competitors
Embeddable widget with independent ratings for restaurant websites
antiFeatures: No own delivery service
No restaurant advertising revenue
No paid rating improvements
food-delivery-5.monetization: Restaurant subscription to the analytics panel. Restaurants already pay marketing teams to manage their reputation and have no access to honest data. White-label licensing for trade publications and restaurant associations.

food-delivery-6.title: Order Direct
food-delivery-6.oneLiner: SaaS for restaurants: accept delivery orders directly through your website or messenger for a fixed monthly fee instead of a 30% aggregator cut
food-delivery-6.gap: Restaurants pay DoorDash or Uber Eats 30% of every order. On an average check of twenty-five dollars that is seven-fifty in fees, on top of kitchen margins that are already only ten to fifteen percent.
food-delivery-6.pitch: An ordering widget for the restaurant website and a bot in WhatsApp or Telegram for taking orders without a middleman. The restaurant pays a flat subscription, not a percentage of revenue. Setup takes ten minutes: menu imported from Google Sheets or a POS like IIKO or R-Keeper, payments via Stripe or YooKassa. Independent restaurants and ghost kitchens already hate aggregators and are actively looking for a way out.
features: Order widget for the restaurant website, embedded as an iframe
WhatsApp and Telegram bot with menu and payment built in
POS integration (IIKO, R-Keeper, iPos) to automatically route orders to the kitchen
Automatic courier dispatch via Yandex Delivery or the restaurant's own fleet
Order analytics: peak hours, top dishes, refund rate
antiFeatures: No marketplace for customers to discover new restaurants
No percentage-based commission on revenue
No proprietary courier fleet
food-delivery-6.monetization: Monthly restaurant subscription. Restaurants already pay aggregators and are ready to pay for a tool that cuts that line item. Additional revenue from POS integration setup and maintenance.

food-delivery-7.title: Lunch Subscription
food-delivery-7.oneLiner: A subscription service for daily lunches from one nearby restaurant: choose it once, the menu changes every day, and you pay a fixed monthly rate
food-delivery-7.gap: Deciding what to order every day, picking a restaurant, and paying separate delivery fees is decision fatigue on top of unpredictable costs. Platform fees add up to fifty percent of the food price.
food-delivery-7.pitch: A person subscribes to lunch deliveries from a specific restaurant near their home or office. The monthly menu is known in advance and they can exclude dishes or allergens when they sign up. The restaurant gets a predictable order flow and can optimize purchasing. The customer saves on fees and the restaurant saves on marketing. There is no need to compete on a marketplace because this is a long-term relationship between a specific restaurant and its loyal regulars.
features: Restaurant finder by location with a preview of the weekly menu
Fixed monthly price with no variable fees or delivery surcharges
Allergen and disliked dish exclusions set at signup
Evening notification about tomorrow's meal with the option to skip a day
Loyalty points that accumulate when the subscription is renewed for multiple months
antiFeatures: No choice from hundreds of restaurants on every order
No one-off orders without a subscription
No dinner or breakfast delivery in the first version
food-delivery-7.monetization: Monthly customer subscription at a fixed price. A small platform markup over food cost (10% instead of 30%). Restaurants pay a subscription for menu management and subscriber analytics. Customers already buy lunch every day and want to reduce the fee overhead.

music-streaming-1.title: Licensed Music for Venues
music-streaming-1.oneLiner: A B2B service for legal background music in restaurants, shops, and salons transparent pricing and ready-made playlists curated by atmosphere
music-streaming-1.gap: Cafes and shops are legally required to pay for public performance rights, but no practical tool exists for this: either expensive brokers or illegal Spotify usage (which explicitly prohibits commercial use)
music-streaming-1.pitch: Small businesses routinely play consumer streaming services in their venues, violating license agreements and risking fines from collection societies. This service offers curated atmosphere playlists with a public performance license included, a single flat monthly fee, and browser-based management with no app install required. The paying customer already exists and already pays for rent and coffee they just need something legal and easy.
features: Ready-made playlists by venue type (cafe, barbershop, boutique, office) and time of day
Public performance license included in the subscription price
Browser-based management with no app installation on the work computer
BPM and tempo controls to match the pace of the room
Accounting-ready reports with proof of legal usage
antiFeatures: Listener-taste recommendation algorithms
Personal playlists and likes
Podcasts and talk content
music-streaming-1.monetization: Small businesses pay a fixed monthly per-location subscription (similar to ASCAP/BMI in the US, but packaged as a clean SaaS product with easy access). Average revenue per user is higher than consumer plans and churn is lower.

music-streaming-2.title: Streaming Without AI Music
music-streaming-2.oneLiner: A platform for listeners who care that a real person stands behind every track with authorship verification and an AI-generation filter at the catalog gate
music-streaming-2.gap: Listeners increasingly encounter AI-generated music under real artist names in discovery feeds, and no major platform lets them block or even label it
music-streaming-2.pitch: Major platforms are flooded with AI-generated music uploaded under real artist names, and users have no way to filter it from recommendations. This service verifies every uploading artist and requires confirmed authorship before a track enters the catalog, turning "no AI" into a product guarantee. Monetization is built on subscribers who are willing to pay precisely for this they have already migrated between platforms for ethical reasons.
features: Artist verification at upload with confirmed track authorship
Visible "real author" badge on every track in the catalog
New upload filter: tracks without verification do not appear in recommendations
A report button with fast review by a moderation team
Public report showing the percentage of verified tracks in the catalog
antiFeatures: Algorithmic mixes and auto-radio
Content from anonymous uploaders without verification
Social network features and public activity feeds
music-streaming-2.monetization: Subscription from listeners who left Spotify for ethical reasons and are already used to paying. Additional revenue from paid placement of verified artists in curated collections.

music-streaming-3.title: Royalty Tool for Independent Artists
music-streaming-3.oneLiner: A payments and analytics aggregator for independent musicians: see exactly where money came from, where you lost a listener, and which track paid off
music-streaming-3.gap: An independent artist receives payments from ten platforms at different times in different currencies with no clear analytics, and has no idea where to spend a promo budget
music-streaming-3.pitch: Independent musicians upload tracks through distributors like DistroKid, but streaming analytics are scattered across separate dashboards for each platform with no consolidated view. This service aggregates all royalties and listening data into a single dashboard and shows exactly which platform and which track each artist is losing and earning on. Monetization: a monthly subscription from artists who are already receiving streaming payments meaning they are already inside the economy.
features: Connect all major platform accounts via API and report imports
Unified royalty dashboard in your preferred currency with full payment history
Per-track analytics: where listenership peaks and where listeners drop off
Next-payment forecast based on current streaming flow
Export for accounting and self-employed tax reporting
antiFeatures: Track distribution to platforms
Recording and mastering tools
Public artist profile for listeners
music-streaming-3.monetization: Subscription from independent artists with real payouts. Additional revenue: a percentage of "lost" royalties uncovered through an audit feature.

music-streaming-4.title: Clean Audio Player for Audiophiles
music-streaming-4.oneLiner: A local lossless file player with external DAC support, USB audio, and accurate bitrate passthrough no re-encoding on the app side
music-streaming-4.gap: Audiophiles store FLAC collections and want to play them without quality loss through an external DAC, but streaming apps silently transcode the stream and do not support USB audio on mobile devices
music-streaming-4.pitch: Streaming services promise lossless quality but silently downgrade it on some devices, do not support external DACs, and hide the actual playback bitrate. This service positions itself as a local file player with honest output via USB and Bluetooth aptX HD, displays the real format in real time, and does not touch the stream on its way to the DAC. Audiophiles have already spent thousands on hardware and are willing to pay for software that lets that hardware do its job.
features: FLAC, WAV, and DSD playback at real bitrate with no re-encoding
USB audio and external DAC support on Android and iOS
Real-time display of the current track's format and bitrate in the player
Local library with automatic tag-based organization
Equalizer with a bypass mode for listeners who want zero processing
antiFeatures: Streaming catalog and recommendations
Social features and sharing
Automatic app updates without user permission
music-streaming-4.monetization: One-time app purchase plus optional subscription for cloud library sync. The audience already spends freely on hardware and does not cut corners on software.

music-streaming-5.title: Kids Music Subscription
music-streaming-5.oneLiner: A children's music streaming service for parents: a curated catalog with no adult content, no ads, and parental control over the playback queue
music-streaming-5.gap: Parents play music for their children through a shared Spotify or YouTube Music account, but the algorithm mixes in adult content, ads, and videos that are not meant for kids
music-streaming-5.pitch: Parents already pay for kids streaming in video (Netflix Kids, YouTube Kids), but there is no equivalent for audio with real controls. This service is built around a curated catalog of children's songs, classics, and audio stories with no ads, and a mode where children can only choose from a parent-approved list. The audience already pays for children's subscriptions in video and books extending that pattern to audio is a natural next step.
features: Curated catalog of children's music, classics, and audio stories with no adult content
Child mode: children hear only what a parent has added to the list
No ads and no auto-transition to recommendations outside the approved list
Offline downloads for travel that work without connection errors
One family account with separate profiles for each child
antiFeatures: Open catalog without content filtering
Recommendation algorithm without parental approval
Social features and public profiles for children
music-streaming-5.monetization: Monthly family subscription. Parents already pay for Netflix Kids, Storytel, and children's apps the payment pattern is established.

music-streaming-6.title: Work Music Subscription
music-streaming-6.oneLiner: Streaming built specifically for focused work: instrumental tracks by genre (lo-fi, classical, ambient, biophilia) with a session timer and an uninterrupted mode
music-streaming-6.gap: People listen to music while working, but standard streaming interrupts with ads, mixes vocal tracks into instrumental playlists, and does not allow a seamless flow without pauses
music-streaming-6.pitch: The focus tools market (Focusmate, Brain.fm, Forest) is established and pays well, but the music segment is either Brain.fm at a premium price or generic Spotify with the wrong UX. This service offers curated vocal-free streams with a work session timer (Pomodoro or custom) and a do-not-disturb mode with no ads or notifications. The paying customer: knowledge workers, freelancers, and students who have already bought Notion, Figma, or other productivity tools.
features: Vocal-free streams by genre: lo-fi, classical, ambient, nature sounds
Built-in session timer with a soft audio cue at the end
Uninterrupted mode: gapless transitions between tracks with no ads
Tempo and intensity controls within a genre for different types of tasks
Offline access to all streams with no network errors
antiFeatures: Vocal tracks inside work streams
"You might also like" recommendations during a session
Social features and listening history
music-streaming-6.monetization: Monthly subscription from knowledge workers. The target audience already pays for Notion, Figma, and Superhuman and does not skimp on productivity tools.

music-streaming-7.title: DJ Set Prep and Preset Tool
music-streaming-7.oneLiner: Streaming with DJ workflow tools: BPM filter across the catalog, Rekordbox playlist export, key-based search, and reliable offline downloads with quality guarantees
music-streaming-7.gap: DJs pay for streaming to find new music for sets but cannot search by BPM and key, do not trust offline downloads for live performances, and cannot export playlists to professional software
music-streaming-7.pitch: DJs actively use Beatport and Tidal DJ, but Tidal DJ is expensive and Beatport is limited by genre. This service is built around real set preparation tasks: search by BPM, key, and genre export to Rekordbox and Serato formats reliable offline downloads for live shows. Monetization is durable: a DJ pays for tools that save hours of prep and reduce the risk of a technical failure at an event.
features: Catalog search with BPM, key, genre, and year filters
Playlist export to XML for Rekordbox and Serato
Offline downloads with file verification before a performance
Next-track suggestions by key (harmonic mixing)
Set history with the ability to restore a previous playlist
antiFeatures: Listener-taste based recommendations
Podcasts and talk content
Social profile for public track sharing
music-streaming-7.monetization: Subscription from professional and semi-professional DJs. The audience already pays for Beatport, Rekordbox, and DJ controllers the habit of paying for tools is fully formed.

video-streaming-1.title: Ad-Free Player for Catalog Content
video-streaming-1.oneLiner: A B2B tool for owners of archive and niche content: a white-label player with a genuinely ad-free model and clear retention analytics.
video-streaming-1.gap: Studios and distributors with archive libraries cannot sell content directly without building their own player and billing stack. They are forced to hand their catalogs to platforms that cut them with ads and compete for the same viewers.
video-streaming-1.pitch: A rights holder sitting on 500 old films or niche series gets a ready-made player under their own brand, built-in billing, offline viewing, and an analytics dashboard. No engineering team required and no ads running over someone else's content. The service takes a fixed percentage of each subscription, the studio stays in control, and nobody is at the mercy of Netflix algorithms.
features: White-label player: custom branding, domain, and mobile apps delivered turnkey
Built-in billing: subscriptions, single rentals, bundles, and promo codes
Offline viewing that works without an internet connection on startup
Retention analytics broken down by episode, scene, and device
Rights management by territory and license expiry date
antiFeatures: No ads over paid content
No shared catalog: every client is fully isolated
No algorithmic recommendations for other clients' content
video-streaming-1.monetization: Studios, distributors, and independent rights holders already pay for hosting, CDN, and license compliance. We take 8 to 12 percent of their revenue plus a base infrastructure fee.

video-streaming-2.title: Billing Auditor for Streaming Subscriptions
video-streaming-2.oneLiner: An app that tracks all of a user's streaming subscriptions, warns about hidden price increases, automatically captures screenshots of promises made at the time of payment, and helps users file for refunds.
video-streaming-2.gap: People pay for a subscription and get a different product: ads added to a premium tier, content pulled from the catalog, terms changed after the fact. Without capturing those promises at the moment of payment, proving any of it and demanding a refund is nearly impossible.
video-streaming-2.pitch: The service automatically snapshots subscription terms at every payment and stores them as a timestamped record. When a service changes its terms (adds ads, removes content, raises the price) the user gets a notification showing exactly what changed, along with a template complaint letter for their bank, a small-claims court, or a regulator. Monetization is a monthly subscription the user recoups with their very first successful chargeback.
features: Timestamped snapshot of subscription terms at every payment
Notification of term changes with a precise diff of what changed
Auto-generated complaint templates for the bank, Apple or Google, and regulators
Tracker of all active subscriptions with real monthly cost
Refund history and success-rate stats for chargebacks by service
antiFeatures: Not a streaming comparison tool (this is an auditor, not an aggregator)
No best-deal suggestions or affiliate links
No collection of viewing data for ad profiling
video-streaming-2.monetization: Users already pay for streaming and are angry about hidden charges. Subscription at 3 to 5 dollars per month. Additional revenue: legal partners take a cut of won chargebacks.

video-streaming-3.title: Reliable Streaming for Major Sporting Events
video-streaming-3.oneLiner: B2B infrastructure for league and federation organizers: technical streaming of big matches with guaranteed uptime, scaling for peak traffic, and financial compensation when the stream goes down.
video-streaming-3.gap: Federations and tournament organizers sell broadcasting rights to large platforms that crash at the worst possible moment. Viewers pay for an event and cannot watch it, and the federation takes the reputational hit with no way to enforce an SLA against the technical provider.
video-streaming-3.pitch: A purpose-built CDN and streaming stack for sports peaks: automatic scaling in the 10 minutes before kickoff, real-time monitoring, and financial compensation for outages. Payment integration lets the platform automatically refund viewers when the stream is unavailable. Sold to federations and media rights holders, not to end viewers.
features: Auto-scaling for peak traffic 10 to 15 minutes before broadcast
SLA with financial compensation for stream outages
Built-in auto-refund to viewers when a confirmed outage is detected
Multi-camera mode without added latency
Organizer dashboard: viewer counts, quality metrics, geography, and incident log
antiFeatures: Does not produce content or provide commentary
Does not sell subscriptions directly to end viewers
Does not take a cut of media rights
video-streaming-3.monetization: Federations, leagues, and broadcasters already pay for rights, production, and technical streaming. Reliability is the value, not low cost. Fixed fee per event plus a seasonal monthly contract.

video-streaming-4.title: Playback Progress Sync SDK for Streaming Apps
video-streaming-4.oneLiner: For streaming app developers: a ready-made SDK that reliably saves viewing progress, syncs it across devices, and manages the playback queue.
video-streaming-4.gap: Product teams at major services have spent years failing to fix basic progress sync and the continue-watching feature. It is an infrastructure problem that everyone solves from scratch and still ships with bugs.
video-streaming-4.pitch: A drop-in SDK for iOS, Android, and web that takes ownership of all viewing state: position within an episode, episode order, favorites, and history. It works offline, syncs when the connection is restored, supports multiple profiles, and never loses data on logout. Sold to teams that already have content and a player but do not have the resources to build reliable sync.
features: Offline-first progress storage with automatic sync on reconnect
Multi-profile mode with data isolation at the SDK level
Queue management API: add, remove, and reorder
Webhook on data conflict between devices with a built-in resolution strategy
Metrics dashboard: progress loss events, conflicts, and drop-off by device
antiFeatures: Not a player and not a CDN: only viewing state management
Not a recommendation engine
Does not handle DRM or content protection
video-streaming-4.monetization: Product and engineering teams at streaming services already spend money building these features. SaaS: priced per MAU or in tiers based on the number of active profiles.

video-streaming-5.title: Dubbing and Localization Platform for Niche Libraries
video-streaming-5.oneLiner: A tool for distributors: upload your catalog, order dubbing or subtitles in the target language through a network of professional studios, and receive a finished file with correct metadata.
video-streaming-5.gap: Small distributors and rights holders cannot reach Hindi, Tamil, or Arabic-speaking markets because ordering dubbing is expensive and operationally complex. Viewers see a language promised on the content card and cannot find it in the player, which directly costs subscribers.
video-streaming-5.pitch: A marketplace of dubbing studios with a single API: the rights holder uploads the video and script, selects a language and budget, and gets back an audio track in the required format, correctly synced. The platform manages quality through review checkpoints, stores the tracks, and lets them be embedded in any player via a standard manifest. A separate verification tool checks that declared languages match actual tracks before publication.
features: Dubbing studio marketplace with ratings and language specializations
Single API for placing an order and receiving the finished file
Language verifier: checks declared audio tracks against actual content before publishing
Track storage with CDN delivery and HLS and DASH manifest support
Automated QA: sync check of the audio track against the video using timestamps
antiFeatures: Not fully automated AI dubbing without a human review step
Does not work directly with end viewers
Not a crowdsourced subtitle aggregator
video-streaming-5.monetization: Distributors and rights holders already pay for localization. We take a percentage of each order plus fees for storage and CDN delivery of the tracks.

video-streaming-6.title: Completed Series Aggregator
video-streaming-6.oneLiner: A streaming service for viewers who refuse to start a show knowing it might be canceled without an ending: only completed stories with a finale, protected from removal.
video-streaming-6.gap: Viewers invest weeks in a series only to have the platform cancel it or silently pull it from the catalog. This destroys trust in the long-form subscription format and creates real demand for a safe catalog.
video-streaming-6.pitch: A catalog of series with a proper ending only: no unfinished stories. Licensing comes directly from studios for already-produced seasons. The viewer knows that any series they start can be watched all the way through and the content will not disappear. The target audience is adults aged 30 to 50 with money who value their time and do not want to risk an unfinished story.
features: Completed series only: all seasons with a finale must exist before a title is added
Availability guarantee: the contract prevents removing a title without 90 days notice
Notification if a rights holder does pull a license, with an alternative place to finish watching
Filters by genre, number of seasons, country of production, and year of the finale
Safe Start: a confidence rating indicating the series is definitively finished
antiFeatures: No original productions: only already-produced content
No live broadcasts or news formats
No recommendations for unfinished series from other platforms
video-streaming-6.monetization: Adults aged 30 to 50 with income already pay for multiple streaming services. Subscription at 6 to 8 dollars per month. The niche is small but willing to pay a premium for predictability.

video-streaming-7.title: Ad Operations Center for AVOD Platforms
video-streaming-7.oneLiner: A B2B tool for free streaming services: manage ad insertions with frequency capping, volume normalization, and filtering of unwanted content categories.
video-streaming-7.gap: Free platforms insert ads every three minutes, the ad block is louder than the content, and it is full of gambling or adult ads. Platforms are losing audiences not because viewers cannot afford to pay but because the experience is physically unbearable. Meanwhile advertisers are paying for impressions that nobody actually watches.
video-streaming-7.pitch: A SaaS tool for AVOD platform operations teams: set a maximum insertion frequency per hour, an upper volume limit, and a blocklist of ad content categories. The system automatically normalizes the ad inventory, moves breaks to narratively appropriate pauses, and generates a report on actual view-through rates. Advertisers pay only for completed impressions, and the platform can sell its inventory at a higher CPM because the quality is real.
features: Frequency normalizer: no more than N ad minutes per hour of content
Volume normalization for ad breaks to match content level in LUFS
Category blocklist: gambling, alcohol, adult content, and others
Narrative pause detection for break placement using silence and cut analysis
Real view-through analytics: percentage of viewers who switched tabs or muted during ads
antiFeatures: Not an ad exchange and not a DSP
Does not sell advertising inventory
Does not insert ads into content independently without integrating with an existing ad server
video-streaming-7.monetization: AVOD platforms already pay for ad servers and analytics. SaaS: priced by volume of ad insertions per month or by number of unique viewers. Revenue share from CPM uplift is also an option.

messaging-apps-1.title: Work Chat Without Your Personal Phone
messaging-apps-1.oneLiner: A corporate messenger where employees have two separate profiles in one app, no second device needed and no personal number exposed to the employer.
messaging-apps-1.gap: Employees are forced to either expose their personal phone number to the employer or carry two devices. When someone leaves a job, the work chat stays with the former employer and all message history is gone forever.
messaging-apps-1.pitch: Every employee gets a work identity completely isolated from their personal one. Switching between them is instant, with no sign-out required and no "session expired" errors. The company pays for employee work numbers and the employee's personal number is never revealed.
features: Two independent profiles in one app with instant switching
Virtual work number rented by the company, not the employee
Full export of an employee's message history to their personal archive when they leave
Notification separation: personal notifications stay quiet during work hours
Admin panel for the team: add, remove, and transfer history between employees
antiFeatures: No shared feed or stories between profiles
No employer access to an employee's personal profile
No covert message monitoring without the employee's knowledge
messaging-apps-1.monetization: Companies already pay for corporate SIM cards and Slack. Model: subscription for employee work numbers, starting at around $4 per person per month. Billed to HR or IT.

messaging-apps-2.title: Anti-Stalker
messaging-apps-2.oneLiner: A paid protection service for harassment in messaging apps: blocking that actually works, with human support and court-ready documentation.
messaging-apps-2.gap: A blocked harasser can create a new account in two minutes. The victim still receives notifications from blocked contacts. Platforms ignore abuse reports. People leave entirely because no real tools exist.
messaging-apps-2.pitch: This service does not replace a messenger, it works on top of one. It detects when a blocked person creates a new account using behavioral patterns, automatically blocks them, and builds an evidence package for court. Revenue comes from victim subscriptions or insurance partnerships.
features: Second-account detector: links new profiles to an already-blocked person based on behavioral patterns
Full log of contact attempts with saved screenshots for legal use
Automatic blocking with no manual confirmation needed
A live human specialist who can file a platform complaint on the user's behalf
Evidence export in a format accepted by police and courts
antiFeatures: No proprietary messenger, this is a layer on top of existing apps
No revealing the suspect's identity without a court order
No automatic accusation without a confirmed behavioral pattern
messaging-apps-2.monetization: Domestic violence victims, family law attorneys, and insurance companies handling stalking cases. Subscription from $6 to $18 per month, or a one-time evidence collection package.

messaging-apps-3.title: Business Chat With Clients That Does Not Lose History
messaging-apps-3.oneLiner: A B2B tool: a unified inbox for incoming messages from clients across WhatsApp, Telegram, and Viber, with history owned by the business rather than an employee's personal phone.
messaging-apps-3.gap: Small businesses conduct client conversations through an employee's personal WhatsApp. When that employee leaves, all history and contacts leave with them. Platforms forbid this use case but offer no alternative.
messaging-apps-3.pitch: The business connects one number and all incoming messages from any messenger land in a shared CRM queue. Any team member can pick up a conversation without losing context. History belongs to the company, not to an individual manager's phone number.
features: Unified inbox from WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber, and SMS
Tags, statuses, and conversation assignment between team members
Client history stays with the company regardless of staff turnover
Quick reply templates with variables like name and order number
Analytics: response time, workload, and missed messages
antiFeatures: No proprietary messenger, only aggregation
No AI-generated replies by default, only if explicitly enabled
No access to employees' personal chats
messaging-apps-3.monetization: Small and medium businesses already pay for CRMs, ERP tools, and the WhatsApp Business API. Model: subscription starting around $35 per month for a team of up to five people, plus per-message API costs.

messaging-apps-4.title: Parent Chat Without Outsiders
messaging-apps-4.oneLiner: A closed messenger for family and school classes: no ads, no bots, no random adults, with participant verification through the school.
messaging-apps-4.gap: Parents communicate in school WhatsApp and Telegram groups that anyone can join, where there is no moderation and where children can see adult conversations. No safe tool for a classroom exists.
messaging-apps-4.pitch: The school or class teacher creates a closed space that only verified parents from that specific class can join. Children communicate in a separate area with light moderation. No ads, no bots, no push selling.
features: Parent verification via an invite link from the class teacher, no public sign-up required
Separate threads for parents and students with different permission levels
Announcements from the teacher with read confirmations
Shared class event calendar
Automatic end-of-year archiving with history handed over to participants
antiFeatures: No public participant search
No ads and no monetization using children's data
No entry without school-based verification
messaging-apps-4.monetization: Schools and parent committees pay for child safety. Model: subscription per class or a school license starting around $6 per month. Potentially funded from the school budget.

messaging-apps-5.title: Messenger for Healthcare
messaging-apps-5.oneLiner: A secure chat for hospitals and clinics where doctors can share patient data with colleagues without using WhatsApp and without violating medical confidentiality.
messaging-apps-5.gap: Doctors discuss patients over regular WhatsApp because no viable work alternative exists. This violates medical privacy laws but everyone looks the other way, until an incident happens.
messaging-apps-5.pitch: A purpose-built chat with end-to-end encryption, role-based access control for doctors, nurses, and administrators, audit logging for regulators, and integration with hospital information systems. Clinics pay for regulatory compliance.
features: Encryption with keys held by the clinic, no vendor access
Roles and permissions: who can see which patient's data
Audit log of all messages for regulatory review
Integration with hospital systems to attach patient records without copy-paste
On-call chat with priority notifications for emergencies
antiFeatures: No public doctor profile outside the clinic
No data stored on foreign servers
No AI analysis of patient-related messages
messaging-apps-5.monetization: Private clinics and hospitals already pay for hospital information systems, electronic document management, and secure email. License per medical institution starting around $180 per month. Sold through the clinic's IT department or chief physician.

messaging-apps-6.title: Message Archive Forever
messaging-apps-6.oneLiner: A paid personal message storage service: import from WhatsApp, Telegram, and other messengers into a single private archive that lives outside any platform.
messaging-apps-6.gap: Years of conversations and media files vanish when you switch phones, get banned, or when a platform shuts down. People lose memories and business history not because of their own carelessness but because the platform controls the data on its own terms.
messaging-apps-6.pitch: The service imports messages from all major messengers into an encrypted personal storage that belongs only to the user. Full-text search, tags, and PDF export included. The user pays once or by subscription for the right to own their own data.
features: Import from WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Messenger, and LINE with media preserved
Full search by text, contact, date, and media type
Encryption with a client-side key, the server cannot read content
Export to PDF or HTML for legal, notary, or HR purposes
A unified timeline of all conversations across all platforms
antiFeatures: No real-time sync with live platforms
No sending messages through the archive
No access to another person's archive without explicit sharing
messaging-apps-6.monetization: Users already pay for iCloud, Google Photos, and Dropbox. Subscription from around $2.50 per month or a one-time storage purchase. Legal-grade exports as an additional paid service.

messaging-apps-7.title: Diaspora Chat Without the Chinese Server
messaging-apps-7.oneLiner: A messenger for Russian-speaking, Arabic, and Latin American diaspora communities: tied to a local number, data stored in the country of residence, with no dependency on WeChat or Viber.
messaging-apps-7.gap: A migrant wants to talk with family back home but WhatsApp is blocked there and WeChat is owned by the Chinese government. Viber has become an ad platform. The person is stuck between apps, none of which work properly in both directions.
messaging-apps-7.pitch: A messenger with servers simultaneously in the country of residence and the country of origin, no data handed to third parties. Registration by email, no phone number required. Works where WhatsApp is blocked. Revenue comes from money transfers and calls within the diaspora.
features: Runs through its own servers in both countries with no relay through the US or China
Email-based registration with no mandatory phone number
Free or very cheap calls between users of the service
Money transfers within the diaspora with minimal fees
News feed from trusted local sources with no algorithmic boosting
antiFeatures: No data collection for advertising
No handing data to authorities without a court order from the country where data is stored
No forced AI embedded into conversations
messaging-apps-7.monetization: Diaspora communities already pay for international calls and transfers. Revenue from transfer fees at 0.5 to 1 percent, paid calls outside the network, and corporate accounts for ethnic businesses. Western Union and Wise already have a paying audience here.

shopping-ecommerce-1.title: Buyer's Advocate
shopping-ecommerce-1.oneLiner: A service that takes on disputes with marketplaces on your behalf and gets the money back to your card, not as store credit
shopping-ecommerce-1.gap: Marketplaces close disputes based on the carrier's 'delivered' status, refuse to refund to the original payment method, and substitute real refunds with store credit. Buyers are left without the item and without their money, with nowhere to turn.
shopping-ecommerce-1.pitch: The buyer sends screenshots, correspondence, and a tracking number. Our team handles the claim: filing chargebacks with payment processors, escalating through regulators and public channels. We take a percentage only when we win.
features: Case intake via form: upload screenshots, receipts, and correspondence
Automatic assessment of winning odds before we start
Team manages the chargeback through the bank or dispute through the payment processor
Real-time case status tracker
Precedent library: what evidence works on which marketplace
antiFeatures: We do not take cases under $25 (not worth it)
No subscription: you pay only for a won case
We do not offer general legal consultations
shopping-ecommerce-1.monetization: Percentage of the recovered amount (25-35%), plus a corporate plan for small businesses that regularly lose shipments on marketplaces

shopping-ecommerce-2.title: Resale Authenticity Checker
shopping-ecommerce-2.oneLiner: An authentication service for buyers and sellers on Mercari, eBay, and local resale platforms
shopping-ecommerce-2.gap: On resale platforms, counterfeits are sold as genuine items. The marketplace takes no responsibility, professional authentication is expensive and slow, and buyers lose hundreds of dollars with no way to recover them.
shopping-ecommerce-2.pitch: A buyer or seller uploads photos from every angle before the deal. Category-specific authenticators (sneakers, trading cards, bags) deliver a verdict within 2 to 4 hours. Sellers with our certificate command higher prices, buyers get a purchase guarantee.
features: Photo upload with an authentication request
Expert teams by category: sneakers, collectible trading cards, luxury accessories
Authenticity certificate with a QR code that the buyer can verify independently
Database of verified sellers with a history of authenticated sales
Deal insurance when a certificate is present
antiFeatures: We do not work with categories that have no clear authenticity markers (mass-market clothing)
We do not guarantee a 30-minute turnaround
We do not sell tokens or loyalty points
shopping-ecommerce-2.monetization: Sellers pay per certificate before listing ($4-10 per item), insurance companies pay for API access to verify disputed claims

shopping-ecommerce-3.title: Real Makers Marketplace
shopping-ecommerce-3.oneLiner: A handmade marketplace with verified creators and dropship and AI-generated content filtered out at registration
shopping-ecommerce-3.gap: Etsy and similar platforms have been flooded with Temu resellers and AI-generated content. Real makers are impossible to find in search, and buyers willing to pay a premium for handmade goods leave disappointed.
shopping-ecommerce-3.pitch: Every seller goes through a video call demonstrating their workshop or creation process. A product without a live production video is not allowed to be listed. Buyers pay more, know the maker by name, and receive exactly what they see.
features: Seller verification through a production process video before approval
A 'handmade' badge only for verified creators
Option to commission a custom piece directly from the maker
Filter by material, technique, and region
Refund guarantee if the item does not match the process video
antiFeatures: No dropshippers or middlemen under any circumstances
No listing without video proof of the production process
No gamification or spin wheels
shopping-ecommerce-3.monetization: Sales commission (6-8%), plus a subscription for makers with an expanded profile and priority placement in search

shopping-ecommerce-4.title: True Price Before You Pay
shopping-ecommerce-4.oneLiner: A browser extension and mobile app that shows the final price with shipping before you add the item to your cart
shopping-ecommerce-4.gap: The listed price and the checkout price differ by 30 to 100 percent: marketplaces hide shipping costs and inflate the price in the cart. Buyers waste time and get frustrated instead of completing a purchase.
shopping-ecommerce-4.pitch: A browser extension and mobile app scan product pages on Temu, AliExpress, SHEIN, and eBay and instantly show the final price with delivery to your location. No checkout surprises.
