features: Chrome and Firefox extension: final price shown right on the product page
Mobile app: paste a link, get the real price
Price history for a specific product
Compare the same item across multiple platforms with shipping included
Alert when the cart price does not match the listed price
antiFeatures: No cashback aggregation or affiliate links (conflict of interest)
We do not collect the user's purchase history
No ads
shopping-ecommerce-4.monetization: Subscription for frequent shoppers ($1-2 per month), plus a B2B version for small business procurement teams monitoring supplier prices

shopping-ecommerce-5.title: Live Support for Marketplace Sellers
shopping-ecommerce-5.oneLiner: An outsourced buyer support team for small sellers on Etsy, eBay, and Mercari. Fast and human.
shopping-ecommerce-5.gap: Small marketplace sellers cannot afford a support team, but the platform's bot resolves disputes against them. Buyers complain and leave bad reviews, and sellers lose their rating and their money.
shopping-ecommerce-5.pitch: The seller connects our widget. All buyer inquiries go to our team of real people. We respond within 15 minutes, handle dispute negotiations, and write replies to negative reviews. The seller stops spending time on correspondence and stops losing their rating.
features: Unified inbox across all platforms: Etsy, Mercari, eBay, Wildberries
Team responds to buyers within 15 minutes during business hours
Dispute and claim management on the seller's behalf
Replies to negative reviews in the seller's agreed-upon tone of voice
Report on complaint types with recommendations for improving listings
antiFeatures: No bot automation for responses (that is the core principle)
We do not work with sellers of counterfeit goods
We do not handle advertising or promotion
shopping-ecommerce-5.monetization: Per-seller subscription based on monthly inquiry volume (starting at $25/month), plus a referral program for agencies that work with marketplace sellers

shopping-ecommerce-6.title: Clean Search Without the Noise
shopping-ecommerce-6.oneLiner: A product aggregator with decent search and filters on top of Amazon, Walmart, and Target for people who are fed up with AI and live streams
shopping-ecommerce-6.gap: Search on major platforms is broken by AI inserts, live streams, and ads. Buyers want to type a query and see the full catalog with proper filters, not an animated circus.
shopping-ecommerce-6.pitch: A web app and extension aggregate products from multiple platforms and display them in a clean grid or table with no videos, spin wheels, or aggressive banners. Filters work instantly. Sort by real price including shipping.
features: Clean interface with no videos, animations, or live streams
Filters work instantly without reloading or freezing
Sort by total price including shipping
Aggregates the same product from different sellers and platforms side by side
Interface customization: grid, list, display density
antiFeatures: No AI assistant in search
We do not monetize product promotion in results
No push notifications without an explicit request
shopping-ecommerce-6.monetization: Subscription for active shoppers ($2/month), plus affiliate commissions from platform referrals without affecting result order

shopping-ecommerce-7.title: Fulfillment Partner for Small Sellers
shopping-ecommerce-7.oneLiner: A service that handles packing, shipping, tracking, and returns for sellers operating across multiple platforms at once
shopping-ecommerce-7.gap: A seller juggling Mercari, eBay, and Etsy simultaneously is drowning in manual packing and shipping cost calculations. Platform auto-estimates are too low, and the recalculation eats into profit.
shopping-ecommerce-7.pitch: The seller connects all their accounts and we automatically receive orders. A partner warehouse accepts inventory, prints labels at the best rate, packs, and ships. Returns go back to the warehouse without any involvement from the seller.
features: Unified order dashboard across all platforms
Partner mini-warehouse for inventory storage
Automatic selection of the best shipping rate for each order
Label printing and handoff to the courier without seller involvement
Returns processing: intake, inspection, relisting, or disposal
antiFeatures: We do not work with large wholesale (that is FBA, not our segment)
No oversized or fragile items without special packaging
We do not promise 2-hour delivery (not part of our business model)
shopping-ecommerce-7.monetization: Sellers pay a storage subscription plus a percentage per shipment, savings on rates come from consolidated shipping volume

ride-hailing-1.title: Guaranteed Pickup
ride-hailing-1.oneLiner: A prepaid ride service with real reservations for corporate clients and medical transport
ride-hailing-1.gap: Pre-booking in existing apps is not a reservation, it is a delayed search. Ten minutes before your flight the driver disappears. Corporations and clinics pay for certainty, not the lowest price.
ride-hailing-1.pitch: Companies book rides for business trips, airport transfers, and scheduled medical visits through a B2B dashboard. Every booking is assigned a specific driver confirmed 24 hours in advance. If the driver does not show up, the company gets a full refund plus a credit toward the next booking.
features: Real reservation: a specific driver is assigned to the booking, not searched for at pickup time
B2B dashboard: a dispatcher books rides for the whole team, tracks statuses, and receives invoices
SLA guarantee with automatic compensation for lateness or cancellation
Accounting reports: every ride with a receipt, route, and timestamp in a single export
A dedicated account manager instead of a chatbot
antiFeatures: No searching for the lowest price right now
No anonymous rides without a company account
No individual passengers without a corporate agreement
ride-hailing-1.monetization: Corporate clients already pay for business trip transfers through contracts with taxi fleets. Clinics pay for patient transport. The service charges a monthly subscription for the dashboard plus a margin on top of the driver rate.

ride-hailing-2.title: Driver Wallet
ride-hailing-2.oneLiner: A financial tool for taxi drivers: instant payouts, income insurance, and credit backed by ride history
ride-hailing-2.gap: Drivers earn every day but their money sits frozen in an aggregator account for three to seven days. Passenger cancellations, holds, and high commissions make income unpredictable. Banks will not issue credit without formal pay stubs.
ride-hailing-2.pitch: An app for taxi drivers and couriers connects to ride data from Uber, Bolt, and inDrive and offers instant payouts for a 1% fee. Based on ride history, drivers get a credit score and can take out a loan or buy income insurance against slow periods.
features: Instant payouts from multiple aggregators for a 1% fee
Credit scoring based on real ride history without tax documents
Income insurance: compensation when bookings fall below the driver's average for three days in a row
Earnings analytics: which aggregator, area, and time of day pays the most
Tax assistant: automatic calculation and payment of self-employed tax
antiFeatures: Does not help with finding passengers
Does not work for drivers who are not connected to aggregators
Does not offer credit without at least three months of ride history
ride-hailing-2.monetization: Drivers already pay 20 to 30% commission to aggregators. Fast payouts at a discount to that commission represent direct savings. The fintech earns on the spread between loan rates and insurance premiums.

ride-hailing-3.title: Tourist Taxi
ride-hailing-3.oneLiner: A mobile app for tourists without a local SIM: book via QR code at the airport, pay with any card in the world
ride-hailing-3.gap: Local aggregators block foreign phone numbers. A tourist arrives at night and cannot order a cab. Airport drivers know this and charge three times the normal rate.
ride-hailing-3.pitch: A tourist scans a QR code at the airport or hotel, enters the destination, and pays with Visa or Mastercard without registering or needing a local number. The service operates through partner carriers with fixed fares for airport-to-hotel routes. Hotels and tour operators sell transfers inside their own apps using a white-label integration.
features: Order without registration or a local phone number via QR code or link
Fixed pricing for airport-to-city-center and airport-to-hotel routes with no surprises at the end
Payment by any international card and Apple Pay
White-label for hotels and tour operators: transfer included as part of the booking
SMS confirmation with driver details in the passenger's phone language
antiFeatures: No trips within the city outside tourist corridors
No price negotiation and no surge pricing
Does not work without an existing carrier partnership in that city
ride-hailing-3.monetization: Hotels already pay agency commissions for transfers. Tour operators include transfers in packages. The service takes a 15% margin on the fixed price plus a SaaS license fee from hotels for the white-label.

ride-hailing-4.title: Kids Route
ride-hailing-4.oneLiner: A subscription for regular school and activity runs with background-checked drivers and real-time tracking for parents
ride-hailing-4.gap: Parents do not trust an anonymous driver with their child. Standard aggregators offer no safety guarantees. School buses do not cover all routes, and hiring a private driver is expensive.
ride-hailing-4.pitch: A parent sets up a subscription for their child's regular routes. Drivers go through an extended background check with police and a psychologist. The parent sees live tracking throughout the ride and gets photos at pickup and drop-off. The driver specializes exclusively in children's rides and runs the same routes every day.
features: Driver screening through law enforcement, a psychologist, and a supervised test ride with an inspector
Real-time tracking for parents with pickup and drop-off notifications
Photo confirmation that the child got in and arrived at the destination
Fixed driver on the route so the child knows the person by face
Subscription model for the school year with scheduling for clubs and activities
antiFeatures: No one-off rides without a verified adult companion
No rides at night
Does not accept children without a registered parent account
ride-hailing-4.monetization: Parents already pay for school buses, tutors, and private activity classes. A monthly subscription of 5,000 to 8,000 rubles competes with the cost of nannies and private drivers. Schools and children's centers pay a corporate rate for their students.

ride-hailing-5.title: Fleet Dispatcher
ride-hailing-5.oneLiner: SaaS for small taxi fleets: automatic dispatch, driver tracking, and payroll without spreadsheets
ride-hailing-5.gap: Fleets of 10 to 50 cars take orders by phone, log them in a notebook or spreadsheet, and pay drivers by eyeballing it. They lose bookings, cannot see where their drivers are, and cannot compete with aggregators.
ride-hailing-5.pitch: A dispatch platform for small fleets replaces calling drivers manually with automatic assignment of the nearest available car. The dispatcher sees all vehicles on a map, the client gets an SMS with a tracking link. The system calculates mileage, driver pay, and generates billing documents for clients automatically.
features: Automatic assignment of the nearest available driver without dispatcher phone calls
Live map of the entire fleet with route history
SMS and tracking link for the client without requiring an app install
Driver payroll calculation: rental fee, percentage, and penalties on one screen
Orders via phone, Telegram bot, and a website widget for client accounts
antiFeatures: Does not build a marketplace: the fleet works only with its own clients
Does not manage recurring routes for fleets larger than 50 vehicles
Does not connect to tax authorities or banks without custom development
ride-hailing-5.monetization: Taxi fleets already pay for dispatch software today. Legacy solutions cost 3,000 to 15,000 rubles per month. SaaS at 2,000 to 5,000 rubles per fleet with five times better UX solves the pain and costs less than hiring a second dispatcher.

ride-hailing-6.title: Lost Item Return
ride-hailing-6.oneLiner: A service for finding and returning items left in a cab: an operator calls the driver, retrieves the item, and delivers it back to the owner
ride-hailing-6.gap: After a ride there is no working way to contact the driver. Aggregator support takes days to respond. A passport, keys, laptop, or phone is gone forever even though the driver found it.
ride-hailing-6.pitch: A user describes the missing item and pays a search fee. An operator calls the driver directly through the aggregator or using trip data, retrieves the item, and sends it back by courier. The service charges a flat search fee plus delivery cost. Corporate clients connect lost-item recovery to their business travel dashboard.
features: A live operator who calls the driver within one hour of the request
Courier delivery of the found item from the car to the client's address
Status tracking: client sees whether the item is being searched for, found, or on the way
Corporate dashboard: track items lost by employees on business trips
Full refund guarantee if the item is not found within 24 hours
antiFeatures: Does not work without trip data such as a receipt, time, or app used
Does not take liability for items above the coverage limit without insurance
Does not buy the item from the driver if the driver demands a reward
ride-hailing-6.monetization: People are already willing to pay to get a passport or laptop back urgently. Flat search fee of 500 to 2,000 rubles plus delivery. Corporate clients pay a subscription for unlimited employee claims.

ride-hailing-7.title: Medical Transfer
ride-hailing-7.oneLiner: Scheduled patient rides to clinics and procedures on subscription for insurance companies and healthcare providers
ride-hailing-7.gap: Elderly patients and people recovering from surgery cannot use a regular cab on their own. Relatives take time off work. An ambulance for a routine procedure is a costly misuse of resources. Insurance does not cover transport even though missing a procedure costs more in the end.
ride-hailing-7.pitch: A clinic or insurer sets up a subscription for scheduled patient transfers. Drivers are trained to assist people with limited mobility. Vehicles are equipped for wheelchairs. An operator stays on the line with the patient from their front door to the reception desk.
features: Drivers trained in assisting people with limited mobility: boarding, curb access, and escort
Vehicles with a ramp or wheelchair lock
Recurring schedule: dialysis, chemotherapy, and physical therapy repeat automatically
An operator on every ride, ready to help the patient and driver
Billing report for the insurer: date, route, and diagnosis code for reimbursement
antiFeatures: No emergency calls or ambulance rides
Does not serve passengers without a medical reason for assisted transport
Does not operate without a prior contract with a clinic or insurer
ride-hailing-7.monetization: Insurance companies already pay for transport for eligible patients through private and public health plans. Clinics include transfers in the cost of scheduled procedures. A B2B contract with one large insurer provides guaranteed volume for a full year.

neobank-banking-1.title: A Business Account Built for Freelancers and Sole Traders
neobank-banking-1.oneLiner: A bank that actually understands invoices, post-signature payments, and self-employment tax
neobank-banking-1.gap: Freelancers send invoices through their neobank, but the bank has no idea what an income receipt is versus actual taxable income. Tax receipts, self-employment tax, and cash registers are all handled by separate apps nobody wants to juggle.
neobank-banking-1.pitch: One in three freelancers keeps money in a personal neobank account and calculates tax by hand. An account built for self-employed people combines invoicing, automatic tax receipt filing with the IRS, and tax calculation in one place. The customer pays for a tool that saves them 3 to 4 hours a month and reduces the risk of a penalty.
features: Send invoices directly from the bank app via a link or PDF
Automatic tax receipt filing when a payment arrives
Self-employment tax calculation split between individual and business clients
A separate tax pocket that fills up automatically with each payment
History of invoices and received payments with an export for the client's accountant
antiFeatures: No cashback or loyalty programs that a business account does not need
No consumer credit products, only payment and settlement operations
No investment tools inside the app
neobank-banking-1.monetization: Freelancers already pay for income-tracking apps and accountants who charge 1,000 to 3,000 rubles a month for bookkeeping. This product replaces both: a subscription at 499 to 799 rubles a month, or a 0.5% fee on each incoming payment.

neobank-banking-2.title: A Bank for Remote Teams
neobank-banking-2.oneLiner: A business account where each team member gets their own card with a spending limit, and the manager sees every transaction in real time
neobank-banking-2.gap: Small businesses pay salaries by transferring money to personal cards, and team expenses on tools and travel all go through one company card that everyone knows by heart.
neobank-banking-2.pitch: Startups and agencies of 5 to 50 people waste hours approving and tracking expenses manually in spreadsheets. Each employee gets a virtual card with a limit and a spending category, and the manager approves large purchases with a single tap. Businesses pay for a tool that removes distrust and eliminates the hassle of expense control.
features: Issue cards to each employee with an individual limit and expense category
Approve spending above the limit via a push notification to the manager
A shared team expense feed with filtering by project and employee
Integration with popular accounting tools
Automatic periodic reports for the bookkeeper
antiFeatures: No personal financial products for individuals
No complex consumer credit instruments
No investment account, only operational funds for the team
neobank-banking-2.monetization: Small businesses already pay for Revolut Business and similar tools. Model: a fixed fee per card (around 300 to 500 rubles per card per month) plus transaction fees. The business owner pays and makes the decision themselves.

neobank-banking-3.title: A Financial Buffer for People with Irregular Income
neobank-banking-3.oneLiner: A cushion account for people who get paid unevenly: drivers, couriers, seasonal workers
neobank-banking-3.gap: Someone earns a large payment over three days of work, then waits two weeks for the next gig. The bank does nothing to help smooth that gap. There is no tool that says 'spread your income across the coming weeks'.
neobank-banking-3.pitch: Drivers, couriers, and freelancers live with income spikes followed by stretches of nothing. The product automatically splits each large deposit into equal weekly 'pay-yourself' amounts and sets aside a buffer for the slow weeks. Monetization is a subscription the customer happily pays because they stopped borrowing money between jobs.
features: Automatic income smoothing: each deposit is divided across weeks based on history
A reserve pocket for empty periods with the option to draw from it early
Earnings analytics by day and week with a forecast for the next period
Integration with gig platforms for automatic payout tracking
A warning when the buffer gets dangerously low, five days before a potential zero balance
antiFeatures: No traditional credit scoring, which is useless for people without a formal employer
No savings goals, that is a different product
No investments, the target audience manages day-to-day cash, not capital
neobank-banking-3.monetization: The target audience already pays Dave, Earnin, and Albert 10 to 20 dollars a month for cash advances. Russian equivalent: a subscription at 299 to 499 rubles a month. Additional revenue: small advances at zero balance for a fixed fee, not a percentage.

neobank-banking-4.title: An Embedded Bank for Marketplaces and Platforms
neobank-banking-4.oneLiner: Banking infrastructure for platforms that want to pay their partners fast and keep money inside the ecosystem
neobank-banking-4.gap: Marketplaces pay sellers after a three-day delay through an external bank, losing touch with the money in the process. There is no internal wallet, no balance, no instant settlements.
neobank-banking-4.pitch: Marketplace-model platforms pay a bank every time they need to move money to partners. An embedded finance solution gives the platform its own wallets for participants, instant internal settlements, and the ability to delay external withdrawals. The platform pays to cut transaction costs and keep money inside the ecosystem.
features: API for issuing participant wallets without a separate bank account
Instant fee-free settlements within the platform
Configurable withdrawal rules: minimum balance, hold periods, and limits
A ready-made participant-facing interface as a widget or mobile SDK
Money flow analytics inside the platform for the owner
antiFeatures: Not for individuals directly, only B2B2C through the platform
No retail products like credit, cashback, or insurance
No standalone mobile bank for end users, only through the platform
neobank-banking-4.monetization: The platform pays a monthly fee for API access plus a percentage of payout volume (0.1 to 0.3%). This is exactly how Stripe Connect earns. Target clients are platforms with a monthly volume of at least 10 million rubles.

neobank-banking-5.title: A Family Account with a Shared Budget
neobank-banking-5.oneLiner: An account where two adults manage shared money without friction and keep separate pockets for personal spending
neobank-banking-5.gap: Couples track their budget in spreadsheets or dump everything into one shared account blindly, with no visibility into who spent what and on what.
neobank-banking-5.pitch: Family finances are one of the biggest sources of conflict in relationships, yet banks still offer either fully separate accounts or one joint account with no boundaries. This product gives couples a shared pool for rent and groceries, personal wallets that stay private, and transparent spending analytics without surveillance. The family pays for the tool that ends the monthly 'who spent what' conversation.
features: A shared account with automatic top-up based on a rule, such as 50/50 or split by income
Personal cards for each partner without the other seeing the details
A shared transaction feed with categories but no attribution to a specific person
Goals for joint purchases with a savings progress tracker
Budget alerts when spending drifts without pointing a finger at anyone
antiFeatures: No credit products inside, only management of existing money
No investments, the product is about the family's operating budget
No business tools, only for households
neobank-banking-5.monetization: Couples already pay for Honeydue, Splitwise Premium, and YNAB at 5 to 15 dollars a month. Model: a subscription at 399 rubles a month per family, not per person. The more organized partner typically initiates and pays.

neobank-banking-6.title: An Account That Guarantees a Real Person When Your Card Gets Blocked
neobank-banking-6.oneLiner: A bank with a contract: if your account gets blocked, a live manager will reach out within two hours
neobank-banking-6.gap: The most painful situation in a neobank is when your account is frozen, your money is inaccessible, and support replies with a bot for weeks. Not one bank has made this their main competitive promise.
neobank-banking-6.pitch: Thousands of people lose access to their money for days or weeks because automation triggered a block and there is no human on the other end. A bank with an SLA on unblocking is the first to turn 'a real person in a crisis moment' into a product, not just marketing copy. Customers pay a premium for exactly this: money is always accessible, or restored quickly.
features: A live manager for any account block within 2 hours, guaranteed in the service agreement
Transparent block reasons: exactly what triggered it and what to do next
Fallback web access to the account with no dependency on the app
A 48-hour notice before account closure with the right to appeal
An alternative authentication channel for when a phone or number changes
antiFeatures: No free tier, the product is for people who are willing to pay for reliability
No aggressive credit products pushed inside the app
No ads or marketing offers inside the banking interface
neobank-banking-6.monetization: The target customer has already been burned by a freeze, or works with irregular income and cannot afford downtime. Subscription at 799 to 1,290 rubles a month. Additional: a business tier for sole traders with priority support at 2,490 rubles a month.

neobank-banking-7.title: A Financial Tool for People Working Abroad
neobank-banking-7.oneLiner: An account for Russian-speaking workers abroad: receive a salary in euros, send money home in rubles, and lose as little as possible on conversion
neobank-banking-7.gap: Someone who moved to work in Europe or the Middle East loses 3 to 5% on every transfer home through traditional channels, and opening a local account is difficult without a local address.
neobank-banking-7.pitch: Several million Russian-speaking people work and live outside Russia and regularly send money to family. Traditional transfers charge 3 to 7%, and neobanks freeze accounts without explanation. The product offers a multi-currency account with transparent conversion, simple ruble transfers, and support in their native language. The customer pays for speed and lower fees compared to a bank.
features: A multi-currency account in EUR, USD, and AED with balances held without forced conversion
Transfers to rubles at a rate close to interbank with a 30-minute rate lock
A card for spending abroad with no hidden foreign currency fees
Support in Russian with a real person, not a bot
A straightforward onboarding process that does not require a local address or guarantor
antiFeatures: No credit products, the focus is on payments and transfers
No investments in foreign assets, that is a different product for a different audience
No loyalty program or cashback, the margin goes toward a competitive conversion rate
neobank-banking-7.monetization: The audience already pays Wise, Revolut, and Western Union commissions of 1.5 to 7% per transfer. Model: 0.8% on transfer volume plus a fixed subscription of 299 rubles a month for account maintenance. At an average transfer of 50,000 rubles a month, that is 400 rubles, which is clearly better than a bank.
